questions.prompt: Your task list prints with the columns out of line. Which fix still works when the data changes?
choices: Give each field a width in the f-string, as in f"{name:20}{status:10}"
Print each field on its own line
Pad the short names with spaces by hand
questions.explain: A width in the format spec does the padding for you and keeps working when the data changes. Padding by hand is right until the first long name.
A string times a number repeats it, which is the whole trick behind a separator line.

questions.prompt: When in a project is formatting worth spending time on?
choices: First, so there is something good to show
After the core features work, because formatting changes what the output looks like and not what the program does
Only if you are using a library for it
questions.explain: Formatting is cheap to add and cheap to change late, which is exactly why it goes after the parts that are expensive to change.

questions.prompt: Which of these make terminal output easier to read?
choices: Numbering the items in a list
Putting every field of every record on one long line
Aligning columns to a fixed width
questions.explain: Each of these gives the eye something to anchor on. One long line gives it nothing to find its place with.
